findings.title: ContactView drops the hatch colour that roomLook returns
findings.claim: In §6.3, roomLook returns `hatch: number | null`, which is a colour. In §6.4 the ContactView room entry has `hatch: number[]` (segment endpoints) and no hatch colour. React then has no way to know what colour to draw the hatch in, even though the spec says it 'only draws the resolved colours'.
findings.evidence: spec L151 (roomLook hatch is a colour), L163 (rooms: { label, points, fill, stroke, hatch: number[] }), L168; tacticalLayer.ts:L133, L138, L140, L144 (the hatch colour differs: crew glass, enemy main, used as the segments' colour)
findings.why: An implementer has to guess the colour or hard-code CRT.main. That breaks 'room looks equal roomLook', and the contactModel test cannot check the hatch colour.
findings.fix: Add `hatchColour: number | null` to each room (or make it `hatch: { colour: number; segments: number[] } | null`). Extend the contactModel test to assert it equals roomLook(false, level, phase).hatch.

findings.title: The per-frame order of click, sync, reserveRight and the console view is circular as written
findings.claim: §3 defines shown using 'the frame's console view'. In scene.ts that view is built after tacticalModel, because consoleModel takes overlayView from the model. §4.1, though, makes the tacticalModel input's reserveRight depend on shown. §6.2 runs pickShip on that same input, and §6.5 orders the steps as click, sync, contactModel, frame, without placing tacticalModel or consoleModel among them. Taken literally, shown needs the console view, which needs the model, which needs reserveRight, which needs shown.
findings.evidence: spec L24, L67, L143, L173-L177; scene.ts:L110 (hidden), L124-L128 (the input with its reserves, then tacticalModel), L133 (consoleModel after the model, using overlayView)
findings.why: Two implementers would break the cycle differently. One option uses last frame's shown for the reserve, which puts the arrows under the window for one frame. The other builds the tactical input twice. A subagent would have to invent the order.
findings.fix: Give the order explicitly. (1) Compute hidden and the station from consoleHidden plus seatOf; consoleModel's station does not depend on overlay. (2) Take the click and run pickShip on the camera, prev and alpha; pickShip reads no reserves. (3) Run controller.sync. (4) Build the tactical input with reserveRight 324 if shown, else CONSOLE_RESERVE.right. (5) Run tacticalModel, consoleModel and contactModel, then write the frame.

findings.title: The key intercept rule contradicts itself for T, and it never says where the intercept gets the station and target
findings.claim: §6.2 says the intercept 'returns false unless the window was shown on the last drawn frame'. The next sentence says that when it isn't shown but the console is Helm or Weapons, KeyT calls toggle(target) and returns true. §6.5 says sync records only whether the window was shown. Nothing says where the intercept reads last frame's station or `state.systems[CREW_SLOT].target`.
findings.evidence: spec L137, L179, L31; input.ts:L63-L67 (the keydown runs outside the frame); duelMode.ts:L74 (scene.draw returns the station to the mode)
findings.why: Read the first sentence literally and T never opens the window. Read the second and T opens it only if the intercept has a station. Without a named source, the plan has to invent one, and online the duel replica is read differently.
findings.fix: Reword it: 'Escape is taken only while shown; KeyT is taken while shown (close) or while the last frame's console station was helm or weapons (toggle).' Have sync record `station` and `target` (pass `target: state.systems[CREW_SLOT].target`), and have the intercept read them from the controller. Add a controller test: T on a hidden console returns false.
